name: pagination
description: Offset, page-number and keyset pagination: clamped requests, signed cursors, page ranges for UIs, Link headers and JSON envelopes

api.name: Page
api.sig: pub type Page[T] = {items: List[T], total: Int, limit: Int, offset: Int, next: Opt[Int]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A page of `items` out of `total`, starting at `offset`; `next` is the offset of the next page.

api.name: PageReq
api.sig: pub type PageReq = {limit: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 100, offset: Int where _ >= 0} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A checked page request.

api.name: request
api.sig: fn request(limit: Opt[Int], offset: Opt[Int]) -> PageReq
api.doc:
The page request for query parameters that may be missing or out of range: `limit` defaults to
20 and is kept within 1 to 100, `offset` defaults to 0 and is never negative.

api.name: page
api.sig: fn page[T](items: List[T], total: Int, r: PageReq) -> Page[T]
api.doc: The page of `items` (already limited by the query) for request `r` out of `total` rows.

api.name: prev
api.sig: fn prev[T](p: Page[T]) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc: The offset of the page before `p`, if there is one.

api.sig: pub type Page[T] = {items: List[T], total: Int, limit: Int, offset: Int, next: Opt[Int]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A page of `items` out of `total`, starting at `offset`; `next` is the offset of the next page.

api.name: PageReq
api.sig: pub type PageReq = {limit: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 100, offset: Int where _ >= 0} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A checked page request.

api.name: request
api.sig: fn request(limit: Opt[Int], offset: Opt[Int]) -> PageReq
api.doc:
The page request for query parameters that may be missing or out of range: `limit` defaults to
20 and is kept within 1 to 100, `offset` defaults to 0 and is never negative.

api.name: page
api.sig: fn page[T](items: List[T], total: Int, r: PageReq) -> Page[T]
api.doc: The page of `items` (already limited by the query) for request `r` out of `total` rows.

api.name: prev
api.sig: fn prev[T](p: Page[T]) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc: The offset of the page before `p`, if there is one.

api.name: Page
api.sig: pub type Page[T] = {items: List[T], total: Int, limit: Int, offset: Int, next: Opt[Int]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A page of `items` out of `total`, starting at `offset`; `next` is the offset of the next page.

api.name: PageReq
api.sig: pub type PageReq = {limit: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 100, offset: Int where _ >= 0} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A checked page request: a page size of 1 to 100 and an offset of at least 0.

api.name: request
api.sig: fn request(limit: Opt[Int], offset: Opt[Int]) -> PageReq
api.doc:
The page request for query parameters that may be missing or out of range: `limit` defaults to
20 and is kept within 1 to 100, `offset` defaults to 0 and is never negative.

api.name: page
api.sig: fn page[T](items: List[T], total: Int, r: PageReq) -> Page[T]
api.doc:
The page of `items` (already limited by the query) for request `r` out of `total` rows. `next`
is the offset after the last item while rows remain; an empty page has no `next`, so a client
that reads past the end (rows deleted meanwhile) stops instead of asking for the same offset.

api.name: prev
api.sig: fn prev[T](p: Page[T]) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc:
The offset of the page before `p`, if there is one: `none` on the first page, the start of the
last page when `p` lies past the end, else `limit` rows back (never below 0).

api.name: Limits
api.sig: pub type Limits = {default_limit: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 100, max_limit: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 100} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
Size limits for requests: the default page size and the largest one allowed, both within 1 to
100 (the range of PageReq).

api.name: request_in
api.sig: fn request_in(lim: Limits, limit: Opt[Int], offset: Opt[Int]) -> PageReq
api.doc:
`request` with your own limits: `limit` defaults to `lim.default_limit` and is kept within 1 to
`lim.max_limit`; `offset` defaults to 0 and is never negative.

api.name: request_str
api.sig: fn request_str(limit: Opt[Str], offset: Opt[Str]) -> PageReq
api.doc:
`request` for raw query strings: each value is trimmed and read as an integer, and text that
isn't one (`"abc"`, `""`, `"1.5"`) counts as missing, so it gets the default.

api.name: ParamErr
api.sig: pub type ParamErr = NotANumber{param: Str, text: Str} | OutOfRange{param: Str, value: Int, low: Int, high: Int} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
Why a strict request was refused: a parameter that isn't an integer, or one outside its range
(`low` to `high`, inclusive).

api.name: strict_request
api.sig: fn strict_request(lim: Limits, limit: Opt[Str], offset: Opt[Str]) -> Res[PageReq, ParamErr]
api.doc:
The page request for raw query strings, refusing bad values instead of clamping them: `limit`
must be within 1 to `lim.max_limit` and `offset` at least 0; a missing value gets its default.
The limit is checked first.

api.name: paginate
api.sig: fn paginate[T](xs: List[T], r: PageReq) -> Page[T]
api.doc: The page of the in-memory list `xs` for request `r`: its slice, with `total` the length of `xs`.

api.name: bounds
api.sig: fn bounds(r: PageReq, total: Int where _ >= 0) -> (Int, Int)
api.doc:
The rows `[start, end)` that request `r` covers in a list of `total` rows, clamped to the list:
both are `total` when the offset lies past the end.

api.name: clamp_req
api.sig: fn clamp_req(r: PageReq, total: Int where _ >= 0) -> PageReq
api.doc:
The request moved back onto the list when its offset lies past the end of `total` rows: the
start of the last page (0 for an empty list). Other requests are returned unchanged.

api.name: last_offset
api.sig: fn last_offset(total: Int where _ >= 0, limit: Int where _ >= 1) -> Int
api.doc: The offset of the last page of `total` rows in pages of `limit`: 0 for an empty list.

api.name: count_pages
api.sig: fn count_pages(total: Int where _ >= 0, limit: Int where _ >= 1) -> Int
api.doc: The number of pages `total` rows fill in pages of `limit`: 0 for an empty list.

api.name: page_count
api.sig: fn page_count[T](p: Page[T]) -> Int
api.doc: The number of pages in `p`'s list: 0 when it is empty.

api.name: page_number
api.sig: fn page_number[T](p: Page[T]) -> Int
api.doc:
The 1-based number of `p`: `offset / limit + 1`, so an offset that isn't a multiple of the limit
counts as the page it starts in. It can exceed `page_count` for a page past the end.

api.name: has_next
api.sig: fn has_next[T](p: Page[T]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether a page follows `p` (its `next` is set).

api.name: has_prev
api.sig: fn has_prev[T](p: Page[T]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether a page comes before `p` (its offset is above 0).

api.name: is_first
api.sig: fn is_first[T](p: Page[T]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `p` starts at offset 0.

api.name: is_last
api.sig: fn is_last[T](p: Page[T]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether no page follows `p`.

api.name: is_empty_page
api.sig: fn is_empty_page[T](p: Page[T]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `p` has no items.

api.name: out_of_range
api.sig: fn out_of_range[T](p: Page[T]) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `p` lies past the end of its list: an offset above 0 that is at least the total.

api.name: next_req
api.sig: fn next_req[T](p: Page[T]) -> Opt[PageReq]
api.doc: The request for the page after `p`, if there is one.

api.name: prev_req
api.sig: fn prev_req[T](p: Page[T]) -> Opt[PageReq]
api.doc: The request for the page before `p`, if there is one.

api.name: first_req
api.sig: fn first_req[T](p: Page[T]) -> PageReq
api.doc: The request for the first page of `p`'s list.

api.name: last_req
api.sig: fn last_req[T](p: Page[T]) -> PageReq
api.doc: The request for the last page of `p`'s list (offset 0 when it is empty).

api.name: shown_range
api.sig: fn shown_range[T](p: Page[T]) -> Opt[(Int, Int)]
api.doc:
The 1-based positions of the first and last item of `p` in its list, `none` when `p` is empty:
rows 21 to 40 of a list are `some((21, 40))`.

api.name: range_label
api.sig: fn range_label[T](p: Page[T]) -> Str
api.doc:
A label for `p` such as `21-40 of 95`, `0 of 95` for an empty or out-of-range page, `0 of 0` for
an empty list.

api.name: map_items
api.sig: fn map_items[A, B, e](p: Page[A], f: A -> B ! e) -> Page[B] ! e
api.doc: `p` with `f` applied to each item; everything else is kept.

api.name: NumReq
api.sig: pub type NumReq = {number: Int where _ >= 1, size: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 100} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A checked page-number request: a 1-based page `number` and a page `size` of 1 to 100.

api.name: numbered
api.sig: fn numbered(number: Opt[Int], size: Opt[Int]) -> NumReq
api.doc:
The page-number request for parameters that may be missing or out of range: `number` defaults to
1 and is never below 1, `size` defaults to 20 and is kept within 1 to 100.

api.name: numbered_in
api.sig: fn numbered_in(lim: Limits, number: Opt[Int], size: Opt[Int]) -> NumReq
api.doc: `numbered` with your own limits for the page size.

api.name: numbered_str
api.sig: fn numbered_str(number: Opt[Str], size: Opt[Str]) -> NumReq
api.doc: `numbered` for raw query strings; text that isn't an integer counts as missing.

api.name: strict_numbered
api.sig: fn strict_numbered(lim: Limits, number: Opt[Str], size: Opt[Str]) -> Res[NumReq, ParamErr]
api.doc:
The page-number request for raw query strings, refusing bad values: `number` must be at least 1
and `size` within 1 to `lim.max_limit`; a missing value gets its default. The number is checked
first.

api.name: offset_req
api.sig: fn offset_req(n: NumReq) -> PageReq
api.doc:
The offset request for page-number request `n`: offset `(number - 1) * size`, saturating at the
largest Int.

api.name: num_req
api.sig: fn num_req(r: PageReq) -> NumReq
api.doc: The page-number request for offset request `r`: the page its offset starts in.

api.name: PageItem
api.sig: pub type PageItem = PageNo{number: Int, current: Bool} | Ellipsis derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
One entry of a page-number range for a UI: a page (marked when it is the current one), or an
ellipsis standing for two or more hidden pages.

api.name: page_numbers
api.sig: fn page_numbers(current: Int, pages: Int where _ >= 0, window: Int where _ >= 0 and _ <= 1000, edges: Int where _ >= 0 and _ <= 1000) -> List[PageItem]
api.doc:
The page numbers to show for page `current` of `pages`: the first and last `edges` pages, and
`window` pages on each side of the current one, with an ellipsis for each run of two or more
hidden pages (a gap of one page shows that page instead). `current` is clamped into 1 to
`pages`; no pages give `[]`. Page 8 of 20 with window 1 and edges 1 is `1 … 7 [8] 9 … 20`.

api.name: page_numbers_for
api.sig: fn page_numbers_for[T](p: Page[T], window: Int where _ >= 0 and _ <= 1000, edges: Int where _ >= 0 and _ <= 1000) -> List[PageItem]
api.doc: `page_numbers` for page `p`.

api.name: page_numbers_text
api.sig: fn page_numbers_text(items: List[PageItem]) -> Str
api.doc:
A page-number range as text: pages by number, the current one in brackets, and `…` for an
ellipsis, separated by spaces: `1 … 7 [8] 9 … 20`.

api.name: Dir
api.sig: pub type Dir = Forward | Backward derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
The direction a cursor reads in: `Forward` gives the rows after its keys, `Backward` the rows
before them.

api.name: Cursor
api.sig: pub type Cursor = {keys: List[Str], dir: Dir, expires_ms: Opt[Int]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A position in a keyset-ordered list: the sort-key values of a row (as text, in the ORDER BY's
order), the direction to read in, and an optional expiry in Unix milliseconds.

api.name: CursorErr
api.sig: pub type CursorErr = Malformed{reason: Str} | BadSignature | Expired{at_ms: Int} | Unsupported{version: Int} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
Why a cursor token was refused: it isn't a cursor (`reason` says why), its signature doesn't
check (tampered with, another key, or another scope), it expired at `at_ms`, or it was written by
a newer version of the format.

api.name: after
api.sig: fn after(keys: List[Str]) -> Cursor
api.doc: The cursor for the rows after `keys`.

api.name: before
api.sig: fn before(keys: List[Str]) -> Cursor
api.doc: The cursor for the rows before `keys`.

api.name: is_expired
api.sig: fn is_expired(c: Cursor, now_ms: Int) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `c` has expired at `now_ms` (Unix milliseconds): its expiry is at or before `now_ms`.

api.name: encode_cursor
api.sig: fn encode_cursor(key: Secret[Bytes], scope: Str, c: Cursor) -> Str
api.doc:
The opaque token for cursor `c`: base64url JSON, a `.`, and a 128-bit HMAC-SHA-256 tag over the
payload and `scope`. The scope ties a token to one query (say `"orders?status=open&sort=date"`),
so a cursor from another query or sort order is refused. Tokens are tamper-evident, not secret:
anyone can read the keys, so don't put secrets in them.

api.name: decode_cursor
api.sig: fn decode_cursor(key: Secret[Bytes], scope: Str, token: Str) -> Res[Cursor, CursorErr]
api.doc:
The cursor in token `token`, checked against `key` and `scope`; expiry is not checked (see
`decode_cursor_at`). Tokens over 4096 characters are `Malformed`.

api.name: decode_cursor_at
api.sig: fn decode_cursor_at(key: Secret[Bytes], scope: Str, token: Str, now_ms: Int) -> Res[Cursor, CursorErr]
api.doc: `decode_cursor`, also refusing a cursor that has expired at `now_ms` (Unix milliseconds).

api.name: decode_cursor_any
api.sig: fn decode_cursor_any(keys: List[Secret[Bytes]], scope: Str, token: Str, now_ms: Opt[Int]) -> Res[Cursor, CursorErr]
api.doc:
`decode_cursor` for key rotation: the token is accepted when its tag checks under any of `keys`
(newest first, say), and, when `now_ms` is given, it must not have expired. An empty `keys` list
refuses every token as `BadSignature`.

api.name: fetch_limit
api.sig: fn fetch_limit(limit: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000000) -> Int
api.doc:
The rows to fetch for a keyset page of `limit` (1 to a million): one more than the limit, so the
extra row tells whether another page follows.

api.name: KeysetPage
api.sig: pub type KeysetPage[T] = {items: List[T], next_page: Opt[Cursor], prev_page: Opt[Cursor]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A keyset page before signing: its items in list order and the cursors of the next and previous
pages.

api.name: keyset
api.sig: fn keyset[T, e](rows: List[T], limit: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000000, req: Opt[Cursor], key_of: T -> List[Str] ! e) -> KeysetPage[T] ! e
api.doc:
The keyset page for `rows` fetched for request `req` (`none` for the first page) with
`fetch_limit(limit)` rows: ascending after the cursor's keys for `Forward` (and the first page),
descending before them for `Backward`, as the database returns them. `key_of` gives a row's sort
keys. The extra row, if fetched, is dropped and only says another page follows; the items come
back in ascending order either way. A page reached by a cursor always has a way back, and an
empty page reached by a cursor points back at that cursor's keys.

api.name: seek
api.sig: fn seek[T, e](sorted: List[T], req: Opt[Cursor], limit: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000000, cmp: (T, List[Str]) -> Int ! e) -> List[T] ! e
api.doc:
The rows a database would return for `req` from the in-memory list `sorted` (ascending by sort
key): up to `fetch_limit(limit)` rows after the cursor's keys, or before them in descending
order for `Backward`. `cmp(row, keys)` is negative, 0 or positive as the row sorts before, at or
after the keys. Pass the result to `keyset`.

api.name: CursorPage
api.sig: pub type CursorPage[T] = {items: List[T], next_cursor: Opt[Str], prev_cursor: Opt[Str]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A keyset page with signed cursor tokens, ready to send.

api.name: sign_page
api.sig: fn sign_page[T](key: Secret[Bytes], scope: Str, kp: KeysetPage[T], expires_ms: Opt[Int]) -> CursorPage[T]
api.doc:
`kp` with its cursors signed by `encode_cursor` under `key` and `scope`, each expiring at
`expires_ms` (Unix milliseconds) when given.

api.name: map_cursor_items
api.sig: fn map_cursor_items[A, B, e](cp: CursorPage[A], f: A -> B ! e) -> CursorPage[B] ! e
api.doc: `cp` with `f` applied to each item; the cursors are kept.

api.name: set_query
api.sig: fn set_query(url: Str, params: List[(Str, Str)]) -> Str
api.doc:
`url` with the query parameters `params` set: earlier values of those names are removed, the
others keep their order, the new ones are appended in order, and a fragment stays at the end.
Names and values are percent-encoded (RFC 3986 unreserved characters are kept).

api.name: offset_url
api.sig: fn offset_url(url: Str, r: PageReq) -> Str
api.doc: The URL of request `r` on `url`, with `limit` and `offset` query parameters.

api.name: page_url
api.sig: fn page_url(url: Str, number: Int, size: Int, page_param: Str, size_param: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
The URL of page `number` of `size` on `url`, with the query parameters named `page_param` and
`size_param`.

api.name: link_header
api.sig: fn link_header[T](url: Str, p: Page[T]) -> Str
api.doc:
The RFC 8288 Link header for `p` on `url`, with `limit` and `offset` parameters: `first`, `prev`
(when there is one), `next` (when there is one) and `last`, as `<url>; rel="next"` joined by `, `.

api.name: link_header_numbered
api.sig: fn link_header_numbered[T](url: Str, p: Page[T], page_param: Str, size_param: Str) -> Str
api.doc:
The Link header for `p` with page-number parameters named `page_param` and `size_param`
(say `page` and `per_page`).

api.name: cursor_link_header
api.sig: fn cursor_link_header[T](url: Str, param: Str, cp: CursorPage[T]) -> Str
api.doc:
The Link header for a cursor page: `prev` and `next` links that carry the cursor tokens in the
query parameter `param`; `""` when there is neither.

api.name: WebLink
api.sig: pub type WebLink = {uri: Str, rel: Str, params: List[(Str, Str)]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
One link of a parsed Link header: its target, one relation type (lowercase), and its other
parameters (names lowercase, quotes removed).

api.name: parse_link_header
api.sig: fn parse_link_header(s: Str) -> List[WebLink]
api.doc:
The links in an RFC 8288 Link header value, in order. A link with several relation types
(`rel="next last"`) gives one entry per type; links without `rel` or without `<...>` are
skipped, and commas and semicolons inside quoted strings are kept.

api.name: rel_uri
api.sig: fn rel_uri(links: List[WebLink], rel: Str) -> Opt[Str]
api.doc: The target of the first link with relation `rel` (compared case-insensitively).

api.name: total_count_header
api.sig: fn total_count_header[T](p: Page[T]) -> (Str, Str)
api.doc: The `X-Total-Count` header for `p`.

api.name: Meta
api.sig: pub type Meta = {total: Int, limit: Int, offset: Int, number: Int, pages: Int, next_offset: Opt[Int], prev_offset: Opt[Int]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
The numbers of an offset page for a JSON body: total rows, page size, offset, the 1-based page
`number`, the number of `pages`, and the offsets of the neighbouring pages.

api.name: Links
api.sig: pub type Links = {self_url: Str, first_url: Str, prev_url: Opt[Str], next_url: Opt[Str], last_url: Str} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: The URLs of an offset page and its neighbours for a JSON body.

api.name: Envelope
api.sig: pub type Envelope[T] = {data: List[T], meta: Meta, links: Links} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A JSON body for an offset page: `{"data": [...], "meta": {...}, "links": {...}}`.

api.name: page_meta
api.sig: fn page_meta[T](p: Page[T]) -> Meta
api.doc: The `Meta` of `p`.

api.name: page_link_set
api.sig: fn page_link_set[T](url: Str, p: Page[T]) -> Links
api.doc: The `Links` of `p` on `url`, with `limit` and `offset` parameters.

api.name: envelope
api.sig: fn envelope[T](url: Str, p: Page[T]) -> Envelope[T]
api.doc: The JSON envelope of `p` on `url`; `json.encode` it for the response body.

api.name: CursorEnvelope
api.sig: pub type CursorEnvelope[T] = {data: List[T], next_cursor: Opt[Str], prev_cursor: Opt[Str], next_url: Opt[Str], prev_url: Opt[Str]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A JSON body for a cursor page: the items, the cursor tokens, and the URLs that carry them.

api.name: cursor_envelope
api.sig: fn cursor_envelope[T](url: Str, param: Str, cp: CursorPage[T]) -> CursorEnvelope[T]
api.doc: The JSON envelope of cursor page `cp` on `url`, with the tokens in the query parameter `param`.
